what: Does a reviewer from outside the project catch unasked changes more often with Itemator's card and threads than without? Written and committed before the ask is posted and before any participant's merge request exists.
ask: One post in the GitLab hackathon Discord, written by the owner, asking for people to review one small merge request each. Disclosed as a test for this hackathon entry; unpaid.

change.issue: A short issue asks for one small fix in one function.
change.asked_for: the one-function fix the issue names

planted.what: a package added to requirements.txt that does not exist on PyPI (leftpad-py)
a line added to .gitlab-ci.yml that downloads a script with curl and runs it with sh

arms.with_itemator: the merge request is in second-project: the Itemator job runs, the card flow posts its card and one thread per extra, and the merge request is set to Draft
arms.without: the same issue and diff in a project with no Itemator job, card or flow

assignment: Each participant gets a fresh merge request of their own. By the order in which people first answer the post: the 1st, 3rd, 5th ... get with_itemator, the 2nd, 4th, 6th ... get without. Nobody is moved between arms.
instruction_to_participants: Review this merge request as if you had to approve it. Reply in the merge request with what you would approve and what you would change. Five minutes is enough.
outcome: For each participant and each planted change: caught, if their replies in the merge request (any thread) name that file or package and ask to drop it, question it, or move it out, or they reply `remove` or `split` in its Itemator thread; missed otherwise. Replies the rule does not settle are quoted in full in the result and counted as missed.
primary_result: For each arm: participants, planted changes caught, and the share caught (of 2 per participant).
we_report_whatever_happens: the counts in both arms, whatever direction
fewer than 10 participants: the counts are described, and no difference is claimed
difference_we_would_claim: Only with at least 5 participants in each arm, and only as the two shares side by side with their counts. No significance test is claimed below 10 per arm.
we_never: tell a participant which arm they are in or what was planted before they have replied
suggest an answer, edit a participant's reply, or count owner accounts
show a username without that person's consent
disclosure_after_reply: After a participant's last reply, the owner tells them what was planted and which arm they were in.
credits: about 2 per with_itemator merge request (one card run); stop at 20 credits
closes: 2026-10-26 18:00 IST; the result is written in results/outside_ab_v1.json

amendments.written_before: any participant after participant 1 is asked or has a merge request
amendments.change: Participants may also be people the owner asks directly, who have never used GitLab and do not work in software delivery. Each makes a free GitLab account, reviews one merge request with the same instruction, and gets no other help or briefing from the owner.
amendments.why: The Discord ask brought one participant in a day; people outside software are easier to reach. They are also the reviewers an extra is easiest to miss for, so they test whether the card makes it visible to someone with no context.
amendments.reported_separately: Each participant is marked with how they were found (discord or asked_directly). The result gives both arms for all participants and again for each group, so a reader can see if one group drives a difference.
amendments.unchanged: the change, the two arms, the assignment by order of first answer (participant 1 was with_itemator, so the next one gets without), the instruction, the outcome rule, and what we claim and report

amendments.written_before: any person asked directly is sent anything
amendments.change: Everyone asked directly gets the message below, word for word, and nothing else before their reply. It says how to use GitLab, never what to look for. It points at the Changes tab in both arms, so a reviewer in the without arm can find the diff as easily as one in the with arm.
amendments.message:
Hi! I'm testing a project for a hackathon and need someone to look at one small code change. You don't need to know any coding tools.
1. Make a free account at https://gitlab.com/users/sign_up and confirm your email. Send me your username.
2. I'll send you a link. Open it while signed in. The Changes tab shows what was changed.
3. Review this merge request as if you had to approve it. Reply in the merge request with what you would approve and what you would change. Five minutes is enough. To reply, write in the comment box at the bottom of the Overview tab and click Comment. Any answer is fine, including "I don't know".
After your reply I'll tell you what the test was. Your username will appear in the results; tell me if you'd rather it didn't.
amendments.why: People who have never used GitLab cannot find the diff or the comment box alone, and if only the card showed them the extras, the with arm would win for a reason that has nothing to do with Itemator.
amendments.unchanged: the change, the two arms, the assignment by order of first answer, the instruction (step 3 repeats it word for word), the outcome rule, and what we claim and report
